editorial: Picture a ten‑year‑old who thinks the monster under her bed is the most dangerous threat of all – and suddenly you’re front‑row to a twisted, darkly comic psychological thriller called Dust Bunny. What sets it apart is that the neighbor turned hitman must fight both human assassins and the creature herself, making the stakes feel literally and figuratively all‑encompassing. Phoenix delivers an almost monologue performance that turns each shadowed corridor into a stage of dread. If you enjoy off‑beat thrillers that blur reality and horror, this is a movie you should not miss. A mid‑movie pacing slip can feel clunky, briefly pulling you out of that eerie immersion.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of psychological thrillers who enjoy non‑linear storytelling.
